I'm going to get so much hate for this, but then again, I don't know anyone else who has memorised the 48 known Amyrlin Seats either.

I found Mat's storyline murderingly boring throughout books... well... what is it? 7-10 or so? Yes, that would be it. When Tuon finally accepted the marriage, things calmed down. Because the Seanchan were out of the picture, at least for a while.

Yes, I house a deeply rooted hatred for the Seanchan. And yes, the POVs I've enjoyed the very most are the Aes Sedai ones; Egwene and Siuan in particular, but also the tidbits given by Moiraine and Romanda, or any either Aes Sedai, in fact. Furthermore, I don't agree with Sanderson's partisan view of Cadsuane. He portrays her far more negatively than Mr. Jordan ever did. 

Likewise, Perrin's storyline was all okay up to Towers of Midnight, where it takes on a point of boredom hence unknown. Yes, he finds himself at the end. That's lovely. But it was still a good 450 pages to go until we came that far.

In fact, I'd go so far as call ToM the least satisfying book of all. If it weren't for Moiraine's rescue and Rand's WONDERFUL zenbuddhist style, I'd have skipped it.

BUT, to answer the question: yes, on the reread I started to appreciate Mat's storyline more. I also took in further Aes Sedai impressions, and on the reread became really fascinated by what is now my favourite subplot, the Black Ajah Hunters. Yes, I created their page here. So yes, I became far more appealed to Mat on the reread. Egwene's story still remains my favourite.

Apart from that, I must say, Sanderson made a wonderful job in adding POVs throughout AMOL. I absolutely fell in love with my favourite cute couple, Pevara and Androl.
